bull_case: Lilly is reinvesting most operating cash into manufacturing and R&D while earnings and owner cash flow scale rapidly. Successor metabolic assets and other therapeutic areas provide a long runway.
bear_case: Current returns are inflated by extraordinary tirzepatide growth. Acquired IPR&D and M&A are economically recurring, and future pipeline failures or pricing pressure could make today's high reinvestment look much less productive.
thesis: RF clears Compounder thresholds but with important normalization caveats. TTM OCF is ~$28.08B, capex ~$9.89B and internal R&D ~$14.60B, so internal reinvestment absorption is ~87.2%. A rough 2024→2025 incremental net-income / incremental debt+equity proxy is ~48%, well above the 9% hurdle, though not a formal ROIC. TTM CFO-capex/share nearly doubled versus FY2025, but acquisitions and acquired IPR&D mean plain FCF overstates true owner economics.

evidence.claim: TTM OCF is ~$28.083B, capex ~$9.893B and internal R&D ~$14.596B, giving (capex+R&D)/OCF of ~87.2%.
From 2024 to 2025 net income increased by ~$10.05B while debt plus equity increased by ~$21.12B; the simple incremental earnings/capital proxy is ~47.6%. This is directional, not formal ROIC.
TTM CFO-capex proxy is ~$18.19B, about $20.35/share, versus FY2025 ~$8.97B or ~$9.98/share. The jump includes working-capital normalization and should not be extrapolated mechanically.
TTM cash purchases of in-process R&D are roughly $4.63B and H1 2026 acquisitions were $9.805B, showing material pharmaceutical reinvestment occurs outside CFO-capex.
H1 2026 net income increased 72% to $14.491B while internal R&D rose 21% and gross margin percentage improved, evidence that current reinvestment is producing substantial earnings growth.

counterevidence: The incremental-return proxy mixes debt-funded acquisitions, working capital and retained earnings and is not a formal ROIC calculation.
Acquired IPR&D and acquisitions are economically recurring for pharma and reduce owner cash available beyond CFO-capex.
Current growth is unusually concentrated in tirzepatide and may normalize.
Manufacturing assets could be underutilized if obesity demand or reimbursement disappoints.
unknowns: Normalized maintenance capex after capacity expansion.
Long-run return on 2025-26 acquisitions and acquired IPR&D.
Owner FCF/share after including a normalized external-R&D/M&A reinvestment charge.
Post-launch economics of orforglipron and retatrutide.
falsifiers: Owner FCF/share fails to grow as capacity projects mature.
Pipeline/M&A spending rises without corresponding earnings or asset value creation.
Pricing/reimbursement pressure pushes incremental returns toward the cost of capital.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Reported earnings growth, gross-margin resilience and the rough incremental-capital proxy are well above the cost-of-capital hurdle. Measurement is noisy, but there is no evidence of structural return collapse.
Diluted shares are declining and buybacks more than offset current share issuance; long-duration dilution conditions are not met.

key_kpis.name: Reinvestment absorption / incremental returns
key_kpis.threshold: high internal reinvestment continues to earn well above cost of capital

key_kpis.name: Acquired IPR&D + M&A returns
key_kpis.threshold: external pipeline spending produces approvals, launches or demonstrable asset value

next_checks: Post-acquisition pipeline milestones and impairment evidence.

subscores.rationale: The rough FY2024-2025 incremental earnings/capital proxy is ~48% and H1 earnings growth remains very strong, but attribution is noisy because acquisitions, debt and working capital distort invested-capital changes.

TTM internal reinvestment absorption is ~87.2%, above 60%, and available evidence supports returns comfortably above twice the 9% required return. Multiple manufacturing, R&D and pipeline paths remain.

CFO-capex/share has approximately doubled versus FY2025 with declining diluted shares, but acquired IPR&D and acquisitions outside CFO-capex make headline FCF less pristine than the cash figure suggests.

uncertainties.rationale: Formal incremental ROIC cannot be cleanly isolated from acquisition and working-capital effects.
Absorption is clear, but some current capacity may be ahead of realized demand.
External R&D/M&A are economically recurring and sit outside standard FCF.

dilution_metrics.rationale: Q2 diluted shares declined ~0.68% YoY while the TTM CFO-capex/share proxy rose sharply; no structural equity financing need is evident.
